newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen sent reeling by tankan shock wave.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen sent reeling by tankan shock wave.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract ended sharply lower on Wednesday due to panic selling after the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment proved much more positive than expected.
"The tankan sent a shock wave through the Euroyen market, triggering almost a free-fall of contracts across the spectrum," said a Japanese bank trader.
The March tumbled to a low of 98.72 from 98.94 on Tuesday.

The tankan showed that big Japanese manufacturers grew much more optimistic this month, marking a clear contrast with the market's expectation that their sentiment may have turned sour along with that of non-manufacturers and smaller firms.

The Euroyen market, bruised by the tankan in the morning, extended losses in the afternoon on the healthy gains of Tokyo stocks and speculation that the BOJ may not be able to justify its ultra-low short-term rates for long, traders said.
In the cash open market, key three-month certificates of deposit rose to 0.63 percent, a high since August 19, 1996.
